Quick infra note — for the smoke we recommend the following config:
- Dedicated staging pool (1x A100 equiv) for the 20–30 minute test window (avoids noisy neighbor effects)
- Continuous batching disabled for the smoke (we want stable latency samples)
- KV cache warm-up: run 200 sequential prefix requests 10–15 minutes before the test
- Max concurrent clients: 100 with 2s prompt TTL

I’ll provision the staging pool and post the load_test_config.yaml into the Drive folder. If Acme needs a smaller footprint we can scale back to a burst-capacity reservation.

Subject: Post-session notes, owners, and next steps — Acme pilot (2027-09-08)

Sarah / Ben —

Thanks to you and the Acme team for a productive hands-on session yesterday. Below is a concise recap and owner-assigned action items. Recording and artifacts are in the Drive folder.

Summary (what we did)
- Walkthrough of prompt set & structured prompt templates (Priya + Sarah)
- Routing policy tests (Karthik): latency-optimized vs cost-optimized variants observed
- Load smoke (Dev): 100 concurrent clients; KV cache warm-up performed; observed 180ms median tail for small prompts

Key takeaways- The latency-optimized variant met your 250ms SLO under the smoke profile; cost variant provides ~2x cost savings but higher tail latency (700–900ms) for worst-case prompts.
- Prefix caching showed a 35% token reduction on repeated flows.
- No security issues raised during pre-call; Ben requested logs retention pattern (30 days) which we confirmed is configurable via the private control plane.

1) Sarah (Acme) — deliver final sanitized prompt set (500 rows) for the extended load run — due 2027-09-13.

4) Priya (Redwood) — draft a short ROI note comparing cost vs latency variants for your use case and schedule a 30m follow-up to review — target week of 2027-09-20.
